channel.title: GitHub Copilot Bulletin — English / Monthly / Devs
channel.description: Latest GitHub Copilot updates for Devs (Monthly, English)

item.title: Copilot Bulletin Monthly #6 — August 2026 · Devs Edition
item.description: August pushed Copilot toward a more open, steerable agent. A cross-client plugin standard, comment-triggered automations, adjustable reasoning, and a fresh wave of frontier models all point the same way: you compose the agent instead of accepting a fixed one. For developers, the day-to-day work increasingly means orchestrating tools, models, and behavior — not just accepting code suggestions.

item.title: Copilot Bulletin Monthly #5 — July 2026 · Devs Edition
item.description: July was about choice and autonomy at the keyboard. A wave of new frontier models landed in Copilot while the CLI, code review, and IDE agents grew more capable and configurable. For developers, that means more control over which model handles a task and more agentic help across the tools you already use every day.

item.title: Copilot Bulletin Monthly #4 — June 2026 · Devs Edition
item.description: This month, Copilot's center of gravity shifted from inline suggestions toward agent-driven development across dedicated surfaces. A desktop app, a matured command-line experience, more autonomous coding agents, and a broader model roster all landed together. For developers, the practical takeaway is choice: match the surface and model to each task, and let agents handle the repetitive work.

item.title: Copilot Bulletin Monthly #3 — May 2026 · Devs Edition
item.description: May marks the month Copilot became a true multi-surface platform for agentic work. A new desktop app, remote session control going generally available, smarter model routing, and Claude Opus 4.8 landing across all clients signal a shift: developers can now direct parallel agent workflows from any device, in any IDE, without being tied to a single machine or model choice.

item.title: Copilot Bulletin Monthly #2 — April 2026 · Devs Edition
item.description: April was Copilot's most expansive month for developer tooling in 2026. A new frontier model, autonomous agent modes landing in VS Code, JetBrains, and Visual Studio simultaneously, and a public SDK opening Copilot's agent runtime to any application mark a shift from AI assistant to AI platform. Developers can now build with Copilot, not just alongside it.

item.title: Copilot Bulletin Monthly #1 — March 2026 · Devs Edition
item.description: This month, GitHub Copilot's agentic capabilities matured across every developer surface — IDEs, CLI, code review, and the coding agent. Agent hooks, shared memory, and a new agentic architecture for code review give developers more programmable control over AI-assisted workflows, while GPT-5.4 and bidirectional MCP integrations expand what agents can accomplish autonomously.
